startup.name: Runtime
startup.one_liner: The AI agent harness for payment teams
startup.description: Platform for fast-growing fintechs to build and run AI agents for payment and risk operations. Teams convert written procedures into specialized agents that work across their internal systems with scoped access, human approvals and a full audit trail. Seven person team in San Francisco, B2B, sold to payments and risk operations leaders.

yc_acceptance.basis: Prior of about 1 percent (yc_acceptance.md, range 0.6 to 2 percent). Up for a team of 7, a precise buyer (fintech payment and risk ops) and strong fit with YC's AI agent interest; technical founders are in 74 percent of accepted companies. Down because agent harness and workflow tools are crowded and the description gives no traction. Net about 2 percent. The company is already in the Spring 2026 batch, shown for completeness.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly say no because horizontal agent platforms are a crowded category and this pitch reads as tooling that every AI lab and workflow vendor is also building. Partners would want evidence that named fintechs run agents in production on payment operations, and without design partners or revenue the wedge into regulated money workflows looks unproven.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2025 --industry B2B --calibration-only: seed 49% / 59% / 65% (cond 59%, n=126). Fintech cohort: seed 63% / 70% / 73% (cond 70%, n=60). time_to_milestones.csv era:2022+ months_to_seed p25 3, median 6, p75 14.2.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Window is 7.4 months from 2026-04-06 to 2026-11-17 and the target is an outside round above about $1M. In the 2022+ timing table the median seed is at 6 months, so roughly 55 to 60 percent of eventual seeds land by month 7. 0.59 x about 0.58 is 0.34. Hot AI agent sector and a team of 7 are not lifted, per the winners test; these odds do not rank this company against others.

bands.rationale: Small post YC round under $3M, as with Diligent's $2.5M seed in 2026 for AI fintech risk operations.
Institutional seed for an AI agent product with live fintech pilots, near Coris at $3.7M and the 2022+ B2B median of $3.5M.
Larger seed led by a top fund for an agent infrastructure story; Sphinx, a close AI compliance analog, raised $7.1M in Feb 2026.
Upside from multiple named fintech customers in production and platform positioning.

ladder.why_it_fails: Seed fails if agent platform interest converts into pilots but not budget. Fintech buyers move slowly on compliance review, and investors will compare Runtime with horizontal agent builders and with vertical compliance agents such as Sphinx and Diligent that already show customers. Finnt, an AI agents for finance company, raised $3.5M in 2022 and is now inactive, a reminder that agent tools fall off when the demand does not firm up.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2025 --industry B2B --calibration-only: series_a 13% / 15% / 29%, cond 26% (n=74); months_to_series_a 2022+ median 28, p25 19.4.
anchors.adjustment_reason: The window leaves only 7.4 months in total. Series A in the 2022+ table arrives at a median of 28 months and p25 of 19; a seed plus A inside 7 months is far in the tail. 0.26 x roughly 0.1 is about 0.03, more than 2x lower than the ever anchor because of timing.

bands.rationale: Smaller A for an AI infrastructure startup with a handful of paying fintechs.
Typical 2022+ Series A, median $15M, for production deployments and fast revenue growth.
Upside A for agent infrastructure with rapid ARR in a strong AI market.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series A inside this window would require revenue far ahead of the usual pace. Investors will ask whether Runtime is infrastructure or a services business, since procedures differ per customer, and agent platforms commonly stall at pilots. Coris took about 20 months from batch to a $3.7M seed, a pace that makes a quick A improbable.

anchors.adjustment_reason: Within 2x of the anchor; given an A had happened almost instantly the company would be an outlier, so conditional odds are near the anchor.

bands.rationale: Modest Series B with steady ARR growth, below the $40M 2022+ median.
Typical 2022+ Series B, median $40M and post money near $600M at the high end.
Upside round if agent infrastructure becomes a category leader.

ladder.why_it_fails: At Series B, which is reached by a small share of seed companies, investors would need enterprise scale revenue and proof the product is not replaced by the model labs or cloud vendors shipping agent runtimes themselves. A narrow vertical focus on payments may cap the market, and sales cycles in regulated finance are long.

anchors.adjustment_reason: Close to the anchor and within 2x.

bands.rationale: Typical C, 2022+ median $74M with post money around $1.2B.
Strong growth case on enterprise revenue at the high end.
Flat or down round if growth slows against the AI platform incumbents.

ladder.why_it_fails: By Series C the company would compete directly with large AI labs and workflow vendors expanding into regulated operations. Failure would come from commoditization of agent runtimes and slow enterprise sales cycles in finance, as seen when Modern Treasury-style tools had to expand scope to keep growing.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Agent tooling is moving quickly and most 2022 era AI agent companies in our sample either pivoted or went inactive. The company must beat both frontier model vendors and vertical agent products, and enterprise fintech sales are slow, so many paths end in a stall or small acquihire.

killers.risk: Pilots do not become production use in regulated payments
killers.evidence: Fintech risk and payment operations require model risk and compliance sign-off; Diligent took about 2.5 years to a $2.5M seed.
killers.mitigation: Sell a narrow audited workflow such as disputes with measurable time saved.

killers.risk: Platform commoditization by model vendors and workflow tools
killers.evidence: Generic agent builders and the model labs offer harnesses; Finnt fell inactive despite a $3.5M seed.
killers.mitigation: Own the permissioning, approvals and audit layer that regulated teams require.

killers.evidence: Each customer's procedures differ, which can make onboarding bespoke work.
killers.mitigation: Standard connectors for the main processors and templates for disputes and onboarding review.

technical_complexity.rationale: Reliable agents with scoped access to payments systems, approvals and audit logs are hard to make safe, but a team of 7 can build integrations to the major processors and ship a first workflow in about 3 months.

takeover_risk.rationale: Large platforms can ship generic agent runtimes within a year, but regulated payment operations require customer specific controls, which slows copying.

evidence.claim: Chargebacks are projected to grow to about 337 million globally in 2026, and vendors report agents handling intake and evidence while humans approve outcomes.
Visa's VAMP thresholds may push merchants toward automation according to trade coverage.

roadmap.goal: Show fintechs running agents in production.
actions: Get two fintech design partners live on one workflow
Package disputes and onboarding review as templates
Close five paying fintechs with audit exports

pros.point: Precise buyer and pain in payment and risk operations
pros.evidence: Analysts handle disputes and reviews manually and human in the loop designs are accepted by vendors.

pros.point: Seven person team is larger than a typical batch company
pros.evidence: Team size 7 from the input allows parallel product and integration work.

brand.name: Runtime
weaknesses: Generic developer term and hard to own in search
brand.rationale: Real word infrastructure names like Stripe and Plaid show a plain word can work, but Runtime is a common technical term and offers little distinct brand; name rarely decides outcome here.

narrative.headline: A well-aimed agent product for payment ops in a crowded and fast-moving category.
narrative.general_summary: Runtime sells an agent harness to fintech payment and risk teams. The forecast window is 7.4 months from 2026-04-06 to 2026-11-17. We give 0.34 for an outside round above about $1M closing in that window, derived from the 2022 to 2025 B2B anchor of 0.59 scaled by timing, with no lift for sector hype. Analogs show both fast seeds (Sphinx $7.1M, Coris $3.7M) and slow ones (Diligent after 2.5 years). These odds do not rank this company against others. Reaching a round later is common for companies with paying customers.

assumptions: Only the input file and market searches were used.
